chunks: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) stoned and did not whip. And they mentioned that Ali (peace be upon him) stoned in Kufa and whipped. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) denied that and said: We do not know this, i.e., why would he impose upon a man two hadd penalties — stoning and whipping — for one sin?

key_terms.جَلْدٌ/ضَرْبٌ: Jald/Darb — flogging or whipping, the prescribed hadd punishment for adultery by an unmarried person
key_terms.حَدٌّ: Hadd — a fixed, prescribed punishment mandated by Islamic law for specific offenses
key_terms.ذَنْبٌ وَاحِدٌ: A single offense — the Imam's argument that one sin cannot attract two hudud penalties simultaneously
key_terms.رَجْمٌ: Rajm — stoning, the prescribed hadd punishment for adultery committed by a married person (muhsan)

ai.seo_question: Can stoning and flogging both be applied for the same zina offense in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies a fundamental principle of Islamic penal law: a single offense cannot incur two separate hadd penalties simultaneously. Specifically, he refutes a report claiming Imam Ali (AS) applied both stoning and whipping in Kufa, asserting that the Prophet (SAWW) himself only stoned without also whipping. This hadith addresses the jurisprudential question of whether rajm (stoning for zina by a married person) and jald (whipping) can be combined, with the Imam's authoritative ruling that they cannot for the same single offense.
